headline: Rust reimplementations and modular pipelines reshape genomic sequence analysis tooling
label: Sequence Analysis Software Pipelines
summary: Recent tools reimplement established sequence analyzers in Rust and add bounded memory, GPU batching, and modular library APIs.
synthesis: The dominant thread is re-engineering established bioinformatics tools for throughput, memory control, and reuse. Two preprints reimplement existing software in Rust: rsx ports RADSex with bounded memory, Bayesian evidence grades, CUDA batching, and Python/C bindings, while rammap reimplements minimap2 with concordant output, AVX512 and WASM SIMD alignment, and a modular library API. Published updates follow similar lines: Trimmomatic adds multithreading, parallel compression, and PHRED auto-detection, and SNaQ.jl parallelizes quartet likelihoods for level-1 network inference. Other items focus on workflow construction rather than kernel performance, including Lift&Add as a Snakemake workflow for adding species to conserved non-coding alignments, AEGIS for GFF3/GTF standardisation, and KhufuEnv as a pipeline-building toolkit. What is new is the pairing of language choice, bounded resources, and composable interfaces.
